analysis.title: Intel Corp. (INTC): First Take: Solid quarter, but very weak guidance on PCs with cautious forward commentary
key_insights: GS expects INTC to trade lower after 3Q26 results because 4Q guidance came in well below the Street. GS says investor expectations were skewed positive on server CPU strength, advanced packaging momentum and progress on advanced foundry nodes.
3Q26 revenue was $16.5bn, below GS at $17.0bn and in line with the Street at $16.4bn. Revenue rose 20.9% y/y and 2.4% q/q.

3Q26 profitability beat both GS and the Street. Gross margin was 44.1% vs GS 42.7% and Street 41.9%. Non-GAAP operating margin was 19.6% vs GS 17.9%. Non-GAAP EPS was $0.52 vs GS $0.47 and Street $0.39.

By segment, CCG (client computing) revenue of $8.1bn missed GS at $9.0bn and the Street at $8.9bn. DCAI (data center and AI) revenue of $7.3bn beat GS at $7.1bn and the Street at $6.6bn. Intel Foundry revenue of $6.7bn beat GS at $6.1bn and the Street at $6.0bn.
4Q26 revenue guidance midpoint is $15.5bn (range $15.0bn to $16.0bn), vs GS $18.0bn and Street $17.0bn. That implies a 6.1% q/q decline and 13.4% y/y growth. GS had modeled 31.3% y/y.
4Q26 non-GAAP gross margin is guided to 38%, vs GS 43.6% and Street 42.5%, a gap of 563 bps to GS and 445 bps to the Street. 4Q26 non-GAAP EPS is guided to $0.25, vs GS $0.46 and Street $0.43.

GS lists four items it expects investors to press on during the call: advanced packaging outlook, external foundry progress and any change to 2026/27 CapEx, server CPU demand and share, and gross margin progression.
GS keeps a Neutral rating and a $150 12-month target. The target applies a 30x P/E to normalized EPS of $5.00. The $150 target implies 57.0% upside from the $95.53 price as of the 28 Oct 2026 close.

market_movers.rationale: GS keeps Neutral and the $150 target after the print. It expects the stock to fall on 4Q guidance well below the Street, mainly from the weak PC (CCG) outlook and a gross margin guide of 38%.

earnings_insights: 3Q26 reported (non-GAAP, excl. SBC) EPS of $0.52 vs GS estimate $0.47 and Street consensus $0.39. This is an already-printed result reported 10/29/2026.
3Q26 revenue reported $16.513bn vs GS estimate $17.027bn (-3.0%) and Street consensus $16.419bn (+0.6%).
3Q26 non-GAAP gross margin (excl. SBC) reported 44.1% vs GS estimate 42.7% and Street consensus 41.9%.

3Q26 non-GAAP operating income (excl. SBC) reported $3,237mn vs GS estimate $3,040mn and Street consensus $2,650mn. Non-GAAP operating margin reported 19.6% vs GS 17.9%. The Street figure is 16.5% in the text and 16.1% in Exhibit 1.

4Q26 company guidance (forward, not yet reported): revenue $15.0bn to $16.0bn (midpoint $15.5bn), non-GAAP gross margin 38%, non-GAAP EPS (excl. SBC) $0.25. GS estimates before the guide were revenue $17.95bn to $18.0bn, gross margin 43.6% and EPS $0.46. Street consensus is revenue $17.0bn, gross margin 42.5% and EPS $0.43.

GS forward estimates (GS forecast, not reported): EPS of $0.33 for 9/26E, $0.31 for 12/26E and $0.33 for 3/27E. Annual EPS is $1.29 for 2026E, $2.09 for 2027E and $4.51 for 2028E. These predate the 4Q guide.
risk_factors: Downside risk: slower than anticipated ramp of advanced foundry nodes.
Downside risk: lower server CPU share.
Upside risk: increased traction for Intel Foundry services.
Upside risk: better demand and share trends in server CPUs.
vol_and_positioning: GS believes investor expectations going into the print were skewed positive, driven by near-term server CPU strength, momentum in advanced packaging and progress on advanced foundry nodes. Guidance below those expectations is the basis for GS's call that the stock trades lower.

tension_points.bull_case: Per GS, the bull case rests on server CPU strength, advanced packaging momentum and progress on advanced foundry nodes. 3Q26 backed it up, with DCAI revenue of $7.3bn and Foundry revenue of $6.7bn both above the Street, and gross margin of 44.1% above the Street's 41.9%.
tension_points.bear_case: 4Q26 guidance is well below the Street: revenue midpoint $15.5bn vs $17.0bn, gross margin 38% vs 42.5%, EPS $0.25 vs $0.43. CCG revenue missed the Street by 8.9%, and GS calls the PC guidance very weak.
